summary: Feed s078_single is degraded: 85.5% of bytes are encrypted, exceeding the IDS tolerance of 60%. All other checks (duplicates, missing VLAN, one-way, packet drops, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding predominantly TLS-encrypted traffic (85.5% of bytes) directly to the IDS without prior decryption. This exceeds the IDS encrypted tolerance of 60% and leaves the IDS with opaque payloads it cannot inspect.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for signature and anomaly detection; with 85% encrypted bytes, most sessions are uninspectable, severely reducing intrusion detection coverage and wasting IDS inspection capacity on undecryptable traffic.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext payload to detect threats. Decrypt relevant TLS flows using a dedicated SSL visibility/decryption capability before the IDS, or filter/bypass undecryptable encrypted traffic, to bring encrypted share below 60% and restore effective payload inspection.
